observations.title: SQL Injection in Product Search
observations.description: User-controlled query parameter 'q' is directly interpolated into a raw SQL query string without parameterization or escaping, allowing arbitrary SQL injection.
observations.rationale: Line 21 reads req.query.q into 'criteria', line 22 only truncates length to 200 chars, and line 23 concatenates it directly into a sequelize.query() string. No parameterized query or escaping is applied. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL via the 'q' parameter. Verification: send a harmless tautology like q=' OR '1'='1 to confirm the query executes injected logic.

analysis_summary: Code-level analysis confirms that user-controlled input from req.query.q is directly interpolated into a raw SQL query via template literal on line 23 of routes/search.ts. The only transformation applied is a 200-character length truncation (line 22), which is insufficient to prevent SQL injection. The query uses models.sequelize.query() with an unparameterized string. The service is publicly exposed with high criticality and direct database access. Facts: (1) criteria is sourced from req.query.q, (2) only substring(0,200) is applied, (3) criteria is interpolated directly into a LIKE clause in a raw SQL string, (4) the service is internet-facing with mixed authentication. Assumptions: (1) the endpoint /rest/products/search may be reachable without authentication (mixed auth not fully characterized), (2) no upstream middleware sanitizes the q parameter, (3) the injected SQL actually alters query results in a way observable in the response. The code pattern is a textbook SQL injection via string interpolation into sequelize.query().
risk_signals: Direct template-literal interpolation of user input into raw SQL (line 23)
No parameterized query or escaping applied
Direct database access on critical path
Mixed authentication model (some endpoints may be unauthenticated)
Endpoint /rest/products/search is available in sandbox for verification
hypothesis: Sending a SQL tautology via the q query parameter to /rest/products/search will cause the raw SQL query to return all products (not just those matching the search term), confirming that user input is directly interpolated into the SQL query without parameterization.
